text: From the study by Bandura et al. (aggression):
A study has the experimental hypothesis ‘Older people will forget more often than younger people’.
This is a ‘directional hypothesis’ rather than a ‘non-directional hypothesis’.
Explain what makes this a ‘directional hypothesis’.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what is meant by an ‘uncontrolled variable’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why the uncontrolled variable of daydreaming was a problem in this study.

text: A problem in experimental studies is the presence of uncontrolled variables. One uncontrolled
variable in the study by Andrade (doodling) was how likely each participant was to daydream.

parts.text:
State the relationship between the variables measured in this study, if a positive
correlation was found.

parts.text:
State the relationship between the variables measured in this study, if a negative
correlation was found.

parts.text:
Suggest one reason why it was more appropriate to conduct a correlational study rather than
an experiment to test this idea.

text: A correlational study tested the idea that the amount of time spent using a phone is linked to
quality of sleep.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe one of these differences.

text: In the study by Piliavin et al. (subway Samaritans), one way that data was collected was by
listening to the comments made by subway passengers. Differences were reported in relation to
the type of victim the comments referred to.
Describe what is meant by a ‘semi-structured interview’ and an ‘unstructured interview’, using any
examples.

Rhiain also wants to know whether babies who are in REM sleep are having dreams but the
babies cannot answer questions about the content of their dreams.
Suggest how Rhiain could observe the babies during REM sleep to investigate the content of
their dreams.

text: Rhiain is investigating how much time babies spend in REM sleep. She thinks that bigger babies
will spend more time in REM sleep than smaller babies.

text: Kylo is planning a case study to investigate the importance of a pet/domesticated animal in the life
of an elderly person.

parts.text:
Rory has chosen to observe the feeding behaviour of some fish.
Suggest one problem Rory could have when observing these fish.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Rory will keep these fish in a container filled with water.
Suggest one other feature related to ‘housing’ that Rory should consider.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Explain why using fish will limit the generalisability of Rory’s findings.

text: Rory is investigating factors that affect feeding behaviour in animals.

parts.text:
Design a natural experiment to test whether a positive public event makes people more
friendly to each other. You may use any positive public event.

Identify one practical weakness/limitation with the procedure you have described in your
answer to part (a) and suggest how your study might be done differently to overcome the
problem.
